soundness_flags.label: Proposition prop:separated-reduction
soundness_flags.one_line: “First-order equivalent to jointly calibrated intervals for the signed cell means” has no defined comparison object or mode of equivalence, and the asserted n^{-1/2} reduction lacks an explicit n→∞/uniformity regime relative to m and xi.

soundness_flags.label: Proposition prop:outer-ate-interval
soundness_flags.one_line: The claimed coverage is a direct interval-containment consequence of simultaneous endpoint coverage and adds no substantive theorem-level content.

soundness_flags.label: Proposition prop:scale-equivariance
soundness_flags.one_line: Every assertion follows directly by applying the stated pushforward and rescaling the already-defined decision rules and loss.

source_verification_receipts.locator: pp. 2–5, Assumptions A1–A6 and Section 4; pp. 4–5, Lemma 1 and Theorem 1
source_verification_receipts.verified_claim: The paper defines the same relative rho and gamma sensitivity quantities, gives conditional max/min envelopes in Lemma 1, and derives ATE bounds in Theorem 1 under its compatibility inequalities.
The paper studies confidence intervals for regression functions under monotonicity and convexity constraints and uses a local-modulus minimum-expected-length benchmark.

source_verification_receipts.version: Public version corresponding to Annals of Statistics 39(2), 2011
source_verification_receipts.verified_claim: The paper studies minimax point estimation of the average absolute normal mean, using composite hypotheses for lower bounds and polynomial/Hermite estimators for upper bounds.
The paper develops adaptive confidence-interval theory for linear functionals via between-class and ordered moduli, including expected-length lower bounds.
The paper gives an expected-length inequality under uniform confidence coverage and explains resulting adaptation failures in density-smoothness classes.

source_verification_receipts.locator: Section 3, especially discussion around Theorem 2 and Corollary D.1
source_verification_receipts.verified_claim: The paper studies de-biased conditional-LP bounds, entropic smoothing, approximation-versus-nuisance-rate tradeoffs, and Wald intervals; it does not give exact-tie finite-sample honest adaptation.
The paper concerns one-at-a-time frequentist intervals for linear functionals in constrained Gaussian inverse problems via constrained likelihood-ratio inversion.
